<user_query>
You are the specialist lane for Sovereign Mag (local companion).

## Goal
Pressure-test a business thesis with maximum honesty. MAG is a local sovereign agent stack that cache-mines cheap inference: a frozen byte-stable instruction prefix rides multiple provider lanes at 96.93% cache hit, cached input is 5-31x cheaper than fresh (GLM 4.5-air $0.03/M cached, DeepSeek 31x off-peak), and it steers cheap models with per-vendor tuned system prompts (CL4R1T4S corpus + distilled seat profiles) so they answer closer to frontier. Thesis: we are a 'distributed generator' like rooftop solar feeding the grid - we generate competent inference at near-zero marginal cost and sell the capacity. Question: is this a real business or a demo? Answer three things precisely: (1) Is 'sell the generation layer' (BYOK: customers paste their own key, we charge flat for the optimization) the right first product vs 'feed the grid' (hosted resale at 50% of list)? (2) Is renting a Vast.ai GPU (~$0.25-0.80/hr, 48GB, open Apache-2.0 weights, ~$2-6/M self-hosted, NO provider ToS wall) the right cheap test of the serving loop, given self-hosting LOSES to cache-mined APIs on input cost but wins on output-heavy work, control, and legality? (3) What is the one thing we are missing that kills this if we don't see it now? Constraints: output tokens are never cache-discounted ($4.4/M on GLM-5.3); z.ai ToS prohibits account sharing and restricts the coding plan to supported tools; free tiers are revo
last_assistant: The category error is the thesis itself: cache-mined API discounts are not surplus generation. Writing the three answers from the numbers you already have.
